phases.title: GPU, CPU and the machine stack

A1.title: AWS From Scratch
A1.why: Eight mechanism families in pure Python, 18 checks. The best first course: no dependencies, every stage is a real failure mode.

stages.title: explicit deny > allow > implicit deny
stages.action: IAM: an explicit Deny wins; otherwise any matching Allow applies; otherwise implicit Deny.
stages.predict: the result when Allow and Deny both match.

stages.title: conditions and permissions boundaries
stages.action: Evaluate conditions and permissions boundaries — a boundary only SHRINKS the permission, it can never grant one.
stages.predict: Allow outside the boundary.

stages.title: STS assume-role: both directions
stages.action: Assume-role needs trust on both sides: the caller may assume, AND the role must allow the action.
stages.predict: identity policy Allows but trust policy does not.

stages.title: objects, ETags and multipart
stages.action: Objects carry an ETag (MD5 simple, part-hash multipart); multipart assembles the parts in order.
stages.predict: the ETag of a two-part multipart upload.

stages.title: prefix listing and delete markers
stages.action: Listing uses prefix + delimiter; a delete marker HIDES a version without destroying it.
stages.predict: what GET returns after a delete marker is added.

stages.title: visibility timeout and redelivery
stages.action: The visibility timeout hides a message; if it is not deleted in time it is redelivered.
stages.predict: whether the same message is received twice.

stages.title: dead letters, FIFO and dedup
stages.action: DLQ after max receives; FIFO orders by message group and dedups by id within a window.
stages.predict: how many times a failing message is delivered.

stages.title: composite keys, query, conditions
stages.action: DynamoDB composite key = partition + sort: Query is within one partition, and conditional writes fail cleanly on conflict.
stages.predict: whether Query can span partitions.

stages.title: capacity, hot partitions, scan cost
stages.action: Capacity: RCU/WCU from item size; a hot partition is a bad key distribution; Scan costs roughly the whole table.
stages.predict: WCU for a 2KB write with no batching.

stages.title: cold starts and warm state
stages.action: Lambda cold start initialises the container once; warm invocations reuse whatever the container kept in memory.
stages.predict: how many inits over six invocations.

stages.title: concurrency, reservations, async retry
stages.action: Reserved concurrency caps a function; an async invoke retries twice and then goes to the DLQ.
stages.predict: attempts for a failing async handler.

stages.title: fanout and filter policies
stages.action: SNS fans out; filter policies match message attributes (AND within a key, OR across values).
stages.predict: which subscriptions a two-attribute message hits.

stages.title: EventBridge pattern matching
stages.action: EventBridge patterns match nested detail; arrays mean OR, and an EMPTY pattern matches everything.
stages.predict: whether {} matches a random event.

stages.title: envelope encryption
stages.action: KMS envelope encryption: a data key encrypts the data, and the CMK encrypts the data key.
stages.predict: what you must store alongside the ciphertext.

stages.title: encryption context and rotation
stages.action: Encryption context must match on decrypt; rotation changes the CMK but old ciphertext still decrypts.
stages.predict: decrypt with a mismatched context.

stages.title: CIDR, subnets and longest-prefix routing
stages.action: VPC: CIDR -> subnets, and routes pick the LONGEST matching prefix, not the first or the shortest.
stages.predict: which route wins for 10.0.1.5.

stages.title: stateful SG vs stateless NACL
stages.action: Security groups are STATEFUL (return traffic is automatic); NACLs are STATELESS (allow both directions explicitly).
stages.predict: why a NACL blocks the reply to an allowed request.

stages.title: the pipeline, and its failures
stages.action: Capstone: wire the services into one pipeline and reproduce each of its failure modes deliberately.
stages.predict: which service's failure stops the pipeline first.

A2.title: LLM From Scratch
A2.why: BPE, attention, sampling, KV cache, RoPE. 13 checks, pure Python.

stages.title: pair counts and non-overlapping merges
stages.action: Write get_pair_counts as a dict of adjacent pairs, then merge_pair with an index that SKIPS PAST each merge, so [1,1,1] becomes [9,1] and not two overlapping merges.
stages.predict: In [1,1,1,2], how many adjacent (1,1) pairs? (two, not three)

stages.title: deterministic training and compression
stages.action: In train_bpe, take the most frequent pair but break ties by the smallest pair, and start new ids at 256. Determinism is the whole point — same corpus, same table.
stages.predict: Train twice on one corpus: identical merge table?

stages.title: rank-ordered encode and round-trip
stages.action: Make encode repeatedly apply the LOWEST-RANK merge anywhere in the sequence (not a left-to-right sweep); decode expands ids bottom-up.

stages.title: stable softmax
stages.action: In softmax, subtract the row max before exp: exp(x - max). The result is identical and can never overflow.
stages.predict: softmax([1000,1001]) — finite, and sums to 1.

stages.title: attention weights and the causal mask
stages.action: Apply the causal mask as -inf BEFORE the softmax, so each row still sums to 1 and position 0 attends only to itself.
stages.predict: the output row for position 0 equals V[0].

stages.title: temperature and hard greedy
stages.action: temperature 0 is hard greedy: one-hot at the argmax, -inf everywhere else. Temperature divides the logits.
stages.predict: sample(temp=0) is deterministic — the tail can never fire.

stages.title: top-k
stages.action: top_k keeps the k largest and breaks ties by smallest index, keeping BOTH tied values.
stages.predict: top-2 of [1,3,3,2] keeps indices 1 and 2.

stages.title: top-p keeps the crossing token
stages.action: top_p keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability reaches p, INCLUDING the token that crosses it (>= not >).
stages.predict: [.5,.3,.15,.05] at p=.9 keeps the .15 token.

stages.title: seeded sampling is reproducible
stages.action: Thread the Random instance you were handed through every sampling call; never touch the global random module.
stages.predict: one seed twice gives the same 50 samples.

stages.title: cache append and shape
stages.action: KVCache stores parallel key/value lists; append, and make len/keys/values reflect exactly what was appended.
stages.predict: the length after two appends.

stages.title: cached output is bit-exact
stages.action: cached_step must reproduce recompute_step to <1e-9: append the new K/V and attend over ALL cached rows — read the cache.
stages.predict: dropping the last key must change the output.

stages.title: the cost model: linear vs quadratic
stages.action: Count interactions: recompute is O(t*d) per step (quadratic overall), the cache is O(d) plus the append (linear).
stages.predict: doubling the prompt multiplies prefill work by ~4.

stages.title: norm and relative-position invariants
stages.action: Rotate each (x2i, x2i+1) pair by pos*freq; check the norm is preserved and dot(q@p, k@p+d) ignores p entirely.
stages.predict: the relative dot product is identical for every p.

A3.title: Context Caching From Scratch
A3.why: The direct continuation of A2: page, prefix-share, evict the KV cache without changing the output. 16 checks.

stages.title: linear algebra helpers
stages.action: Implement the plain-list vector helpers (dot, softmax, matmul) first — everything above is built from them.
stages.predict: the shape of a 2x3 times 3x2 result.

stages.title: KVCache append/truncate/clone
stages.action: append/truncate/clone must keep keys and values aligned; clone must deep-copy rows, not share them.
stages.predict: mutating a clone leaves the original untouched.

stages.title: cached == uncached attention
stages.action: Cached attention must equal uncached attention within tolerance — append the new K/V and attend over all rows.
stages.predict: the max difference between cached and uncached.

stages.title: prefill and the cost model
stages.action: Prefill is quadratic in prompt length; decode is linear. Count multiply-adds to make the difference concrete.
stages.predict: the ratio of prefill work at 128 vs 64 tokens.

stages.title: layer_norm and gelu
stages.action: layer_norm needs a variance epsilon; gelu uses the tanh approximation. Match the checker's tolerance exactly.
stages.predict: layer_norm of a constant vector.

stages.title: generation matches exactly
stages.action: Generation with the cache must be token-identical to the no-cache path — same logits, same argmax.
stages.predict: the generated token sequence with and without cache.

stages.title: truncate, clone, prefix reuse
stages.action: truncate must cut keys and values together; clone must not share rows; prefix reuse must not mutate the source request.
stages.predict: reusing a prefix twice gives the same continuation.

stages.title: block hashing and chaining
stages.action: Hash each token block, then CHAIN: the child's hash includes the parent's, so identical prefixes share one key.
stages.predict: do two prompts sharing a prefix produce one shared block?

stages.title: matching, eviction, isolation
stages.action: Match the longest cached prefix, evict by policy, and keep per-request isolation — one request must not evict another's pinned blocks.
stages.predict: the hit length for a prompt sharing 2 of 3 blocks.

stages.title: matching and node splitting
stages.action: Radix matching walks edge labels and SPLITS a node when a prefix ends mid-edge — test the split explicitly.
stages.predict: the tree shape after inserting 'abc' then 'abd'.

stages.title: eviction and pinning
stages.action: Evict leaves first; pinned nodes are exempt. Walk to find a valid victim rather than evicting the root.
stages.predict: which node is evicted when all are leaves.

stages.title: block allocation and growth
stages.action: The block allocator hands out fixed-size blocks and grows the block table; track free/used and refcounts.
stages.predict: how many blocks a 17-token sequence with block=8 needs.

stages.title: forking and copy-on-write
stages.action: fork shares blocks by reference (refcount++); a WRITE to a shared block copies it first (refcount--, new block).
stages.predict: does writing to a fork change the parent's tokens?

stages.title: exact and semantic caching
stages.action: Exact cache first, then a semantic threshold — tune it so near-duplicates hit but distinct prompts miss.
stages.predict: whether a reworded question should be a hit.

stages.title: cache-aware routing
stages.action: Route each request to the replica that already holds its prefix; fall back to least-loaded when nobody does.
stages.predict: the hit rate after routing vs round-robin.

stages.title: capstone: identical output
stages.action: Capstone: wire prefix + paged + semantic caches together and keep the output identical to the uncached model.
stages.predict: compute saved (%) and whether output is bit-identical.

A4.title: ContextCite From Scratch
A4.why: Which context caused the answer — ablation and a LASSO surrogate. The eval-flavoured course, and the bridge into RAG. 14 checks.

stages.title: splitting text into sources
stages.action: Split text into sources with offsets precise enough to rebuild the full context byte-for-byte.
stages.predict: the number of sources in a 3-sentence passage.

stages.title: rebuilding ablated contexts
stages.action: Rebuild the ablated context from a kept-source mask, preserving order and spacing exactly.
stages.predict: the context when only source 2 is kept.

stages.title: logit-prob math and stability
stages.action: logit-prob = logit[target] - logsumexp(logits); subtract the max inside logsumexp so it never overflows.
stages.predict: log-prob of a token with logit 0 among [0,0,0].

stages.title: aggregation and response score
stages.action: Aggregate per-token logit-probs into one response score — pick sum or mean and apply it consistently.
stages.predict: sum vs mean on a 4-token response.

stages.title: sampling the design matrix
stages.action: Sample a binary design matrix over sources; each row is a kept/dropped subset of the context.
stages.predict: how many distinct rows a 5-source sampler can produce.

stages.title: soft threshold and standardising
stages.action: Coordinate-descent LASSO: soft-threshold each coordinate and standardise inputs so the penalty is comparable across sources.
stages.predict: soft_threshold(0.5, 1.0).

stages.title: recovering a known sparse signal
stages.action: Fit should recover a known sparse signal — check the support and the coefficient signs against ground truth.
stages.predict: which coefficients are exactly zero.

stages.title: end-to-end attribution
stages.action: End-to-end: abduction (drop sources) -> design matrix -> LASSO -> per-source attribution scores.
stages.predict: the coefficient on the source the answer actually needs.

stages.title: span attribution, zero extra calls
stages.action: Span attribution reuses the same ablation samples — assert the number of model calls does NOT grow with span count.
stages.predict: model calls with 1 source vs 4 spans.

stages.title: spearman rank correlation
stages.action: Spearman: rank both vectors and correlate the ranks; assign average ranks on ties.
stages.predict: Spearman of a perfectly reversed ranking.

stages.title: held-out LDS and top-k drop
stages.action: Held-out LDS and top-k drop: measure whether the surrogate predicts on ablations it never saw.
stages.predict: LDS of a perfect ranker.

stages.title: verification and pruning
stages.action: Applications: verify a claim by ablation, and prune sources the surrogate calls dead.
stages.predict: whether removing the top source flips the answer.

stages.title: detecting a poisoned source
stages.action: Detect a poisoned source: its coefficient should dominate, and no honest source should be a perfect predictor.
stages.predict: the coefficient profile with one injected source.

stages.title: leave-one-out fails on redundancy
stages.action: Leave-one-out fails under redundancy — two identical sources split the credit and each looks unimportant. Reproduce it.
stages.predict: each duplicate's leave-one-out score.

A5.title: System Design
A5.why: Optional but cheap: caching, queues, idempotency, rate limiting. Makes sqs/dynamodb in A1 click and underpins the agent half.

A6.title: Dynamo From Scratch
A6.why: The paper behind DynamoDB, in depth: quorums, hinted handoff, Merkle anti-entropy. 17 checks.

stages.title: ring: add/remove/coordinator
stages.action: Ring: place a node's tokens, find a key's successor clockwise, and remove the node's tokens when it leaves.
stages.predict: who coordinates a key between two nodes.

stages.title: preference lists (N distinct nodes)
stages.action: preference_list walks virtual tokens clockwise and must SKIP nodes already chosen, returning N DISTINCT nodes.
stages.predict: N when the ring has fewer than N nodes.

stages.title: load balance and key migration
stages.action: Adding/removing a node should move about 1/N of the keys; measure balance as max/min load across nodes.
stages.predict: the fraction of keys that move when one node joins.

stages.title: strategy 3: fixed partitions
stages.action: Strategy 3: fixed partitions (a fixed Q), each node owns several — routing is a table lookup, not a ring walk.
stages.predict: how key movement compares to the ring.

stages.title: clock ordering and merge
stages.action: Vector clocks compare pointwise: equal, descendant, ancestor, or concurrent — get all four cases right.
stages.predict: the relation between {A:1} and {A:1,B:1}.

stages.title: reconciliation (paper Figure 3)
stages.action: On conflicting siblings, reconcile with the paper's rule and MERGE the clocks so the result dominates both.
stages.predict: the merged clock of two concurrent writes.

stages.title: clock truncation
stages.action: Truncate the clock by dropping the oldest entries when it exceeds the cap, keeping recent causality.
stages.predict: which entries survive a cap of 2.

stages.title: storage node keeps siblings
stages.action: A storage node keeps the value plus all its siblings; a read returns every sibling, not just the newest.
stages.predict: the sibling count after two concurrent writes.

stages.title: N/R/W put and get
stages.action: N/R/W put and get: write to N preference nodes, read from R, and R+W>N is what guarantees overlap.
stages.predict: whether R=1,W=1,N=3 can read a stale value.

stages.title: siblings and read repair
stages.action: Reads collect siblings from R nodes; read repair pushes the newest value back to the stale replicas it saw.
stages.predict: which replicas get repaired on a read.

stages.title: sloppy quorum writes a hint
stages.action: Sloppy quorum: when a preference node is down, write to the next live node and store a HINT saying where it belongs.
stages.predict: hint count after one node is down.

stages.title: hinted handoff delivery
stages.action: Deliver hints when the owner returns, then delete the local copy — delivery must be idempotent.
stages.predict: what happens if the same hint is delivered twice.

stages.title: merkle tree build and diff
stages.action: Merkle tree: hash leaves (key ranges), hash pairs upward; the diff walks only branches whose hashes differ.
stages.predict: how many nodes one changed key dirties.

stages.title: anti-entropy is a union
stages.action: Anti-entropy is a UNION of values, reconciled with the same clock logic — not blind last-write-wins.
stages.predict: the value after syncing two divergent replicas.

stages.title: gossip convergence O(log S)
stages.action: Gossip converges in O(log S): each round every node tells a few peers; track rounds to full knowledge.
stages.predict: rounds for 64 nodes to all learn one fact.

stages.title: local failure detection, seeds
stages.action: Failure detection is local (heartbeat + suspicion), and seeds are how a brand-new node joins without a full member list.
stages.predict: how a node is declared dead with no central registry.

stages.title: capstone: cart + availability
stages.action: Capstone: run the cart workload against the full cluster and hit the stated availability target.
stages.predict: successful-write rate under 30% node churn.

A7.title: Deploy & Debug
A7.why: Capacity math, SLOs, root-causing faults from metrics. The operations thread that every later course leans on. 12 checks.

stages.title: KV cache and batch-size math
stages.action: KV cache bytes/token = 2 * layers * KV_HEADS * head_dim * bytes. Using query heads sizes the fleet 4x too large.
stages.predict: bytes/token for Llama-3-8B (8 KV heads).

stages.title: fleet sizing and quorum tolerance
stages.action: Size the fleet from concurrency and tokens/s, then subtract the failure tolerance R+W>N implies.
stages.predict: how many nodes can die and quorum still hold.

stages.title: percentiles and summaries
stages.action: Percentiles are not averages: sort and take the rank. p99 is where the outliers live.

stages.title: queueing and fan-out tails
stages.action: Little's law and fan-out: one slow dependency multiplies the tail across parallel calls.
stages.predict: tail latency with 10 parallel 100ms calls.

stages.title: SLOs, budgets and burn rate
stages.action: SLO is an objective over a window; error budget = 1 - SLO; burn rate is how fast you are spending it.
stages.predict: the error budget for 99.9% over 30 days.

stages.title: diagnose 6 serving faults
stages.action: Map each fault to its metric signature: KV full -> cache-miss spike; overload -> queue growth.
stages.predict: the signature of a full KV cache.

stages.title: undersized KV vs overload
stages.action: Undersized KV and overload look similar — separate them by cache-hit rate and memory, not latency alone.
stages.predict: which metric distinguishes the two.

stages.title: diagnose 5 store faults
stages.action: Store faults: node down, hint backlog, and gossip disagreement each have a distinct fingerprint.
stages.predict: the fingerprint of hinted-handoff backlog.

stages.title: node down vs strict quorum
stages.action: Node down with QUORUM MET (hint backlog) differs from STRICT-quorum failure (write errors).
stages.predict: which one still serves reads.

stages.title: liveness vs readiness probes
stages.action: Liveness RESTARTS a hung process; readiness REMOVES it from the load balancer. Do not confuse the two.
stages.predict: what a failing readiness probe does.

stages.title: canary analysis and staging
stages.action: Canary: compare canary against control on the same traffic, with enough samples to see the effect.
stages.predict: whether 90 samples can detect a 2% regression.

stages.title: budget-based auto-rollback
stages.action: Auto-rollback on burn-rate, not a single blip — a 30-second spike must not page.
stages.predict: whether a 30s spike trips a 1h-budget alarm.

B1.title: RAG From Scratch
B1.why: Built and ready: chunking, TF-IDF, a vector index, BM25, rank fusion, reranking, citations, tenant isolation, recall@k. 9 checks.

B2.title: Vector Index From Scratch
B2.why: Brute force -> IVF -> HNSW, with recall/latency measured against the exact index you built in B1. The stage that makes 'approximate' mean something.

C1.title: Evals From Scratch
C1.why: Datasets, exact/F1 metrics, LLM-as-judge and its calibration, statistical significance, regression gating. Do this before agents.

C2.title: Agents From Scratch
C2.why: The ReAct loop, tool schemas, retries and timeouts, memory, multi-turn state, failure recovery, sandboxing.

D1.title: MCP From Scratch
D1.why: JSON-RPC 2.0, stdio and streamable-HTTP transports, the capability handshake, tools/resources/prompts, and tool design for an unreliable caller (idempotency, read-only first).

E1.title: Agent Harness From Scratch
E1.why: The runtime around the model: tool dispatch, context assembly and compaction, streaming, retries, sandboxing, tracing. What makes an agent usable rather than a demo.

F1.title: Benchmark From Scratch (Mus)
F1.why: Reimplement the measurement machinery of your own mus-benchmark (2v2 Mus against LLM teams): strict turn-gated engine, one JSONL record per decision, scorecards, calibration probes (Brier/AUC), mirrored seating to cancel bias. Reference repo: ~/Desarrollo/mus-benchmark.

F2.title: Eval Framework From Scratch
F2.why: A reusable eval runner: suite config, metric plugins, judge protocol, significance, and CI gating. The tool you keep using.

G1.title: Compiler + Virtual GPU
G1.why: One ISA, two machines: assembler, front end, register allocation with spilling, SIMT divergence. 12 checks. The right first systems course before real CUDA.

stages.title: instruction encoding round-trip
stages.action: Instruction encoding must round-trip: decode(encode(x)) == x for every field width and opcode.
stages.predict: the encoding of an R-type instruction.

stages.title: two-pass assembly with labels
stages.action: Two passes: pass 1 collects labels/addresses, pass 2 emits with resolved operands and rejects bad registers or labels.
stages.predict: why a forward jump needs two passes.

stages.title: arithmetic, comparison, memory
stages.action: CPU arithmetic, comparisons and loads/stores over a register file plus byte-addressed memory.
stages.predict: the register after an arithmetic op.

stages.title: control flow and error reporting
stages.action: Branches update PC; report runtime faults (div by zero, out-of-range address, non-terminating loop).
stages.predict: which fault an infinite loop reports.

stages.title: lexer and keywords
stages.action: Lexer: keywords, identifiers, operators, with positions, and reject unknown characters.
stages.predict: the token stream for 'x = 1;'.

stages.title: parser: precedence and blocks
stages.action: Recursive-descent parser: precedence climbing for expressions, brace blocks for statements.
stages.predict: the parse of 1 + 2 * 3.

stages.title: v1-v2: expressions and control flow
stages.action: v1-v2: lower trees to instructions with labels for control flow; keep each node's value in a register.
stages.predict: the instruction count for a simple if.

stages.title: v3: allocation and spilling
stages.action: v3: only 16 real registers force linear-scan allocation and spilling to stack slots; mind live ranges across calls.
stages.predict: when a value must be spilled.

stages.title: uniform SIMT execution
stages.action: Uniform SIMT: all lanes execute in lockstep; TID is a GPU-only instruction the scalar CPU rejects.
stages.predict: what happens on a scalar CPU given TID.

stages.title: v4: divergence, nesting, ragged loops
stages.action: Divergence: a branch splits the warp; a mask stack re-converges nested branches and ragged loops.
stages.predict: which lanes are active after an if/else.

stages.title: barrier deadlock and disagreeing branches
stages.action: Barrier deadlock: detect when lanes wait on a barrier the active mask can never reach.
stages.predict: whether a barrier inside a diverged branch can complete.

stages.title: one program, two machines
stages.action: Capstone: compile ONE program and run it on both the CPU and the vGPU — the results must agree.
stages.predict: whether CPU and GPU outputs match.

G2.title: CUDA From Scratch
G2.why: Kernels from vector add to a network. Needs a GPU and a checker wrapper to join codecraft.

G3.title: CPU From Scratch
G3.why: A real datapath: decoder, register file, ALU, control unit, memory and pipelining, simulated and tested. Missing from the repo.

G4.title: OS From Scratch
G4.why: A linux-from-scratch curriculum exists on a branch; port it, then give it a checker.

G5.title: C Compiler
G5.why: Lexer, parser, semantic analysis, codegen, optimizer. Templates and solutions exist; it needs a checker to join codecraft.

G6.title: The C systems set
G6.why: bash-from-scratch, http-server, dns-server, firewall-from-scratch, toralizer, communication-protocols, cryptographic-library, quantum-computing-lang. One at a time; each needs a checker.

H2.title: Inference and serving
H2.why: vllm-engine, tensorrt-inference, ml-inference, sgl-lang. Three are README-only on main; an inference-from-scratch set exists on a branch.

H3.title: Generative models
H3.why: diffusion-models, world-models (10k lines of PyTorch), deepfake creation and detection.

H4.title: Long tail
H4.why: quantitative-trading, spectral-graphs, lean-proofs, haskell-projects, mlops, ml-in-production, sas-lineage-tool, web-scraping.
